articles.title: I love my life and my cup is full but I’m drowning in shame for things left undone. How can I balance it all? | Leading questions
articles.summary: You are not the only one, advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith writes. It will help to ask whether you have a time problem or a bandwidth problem. I love my life in so many ways.
body: I love my life in so many ways. I have a rewarding job, I’m making stellar progress towards a graduate degree, I have incredible friends and community, plus I’m even reconnecting with estranged family. My cup is very full but I still feel grief and shame for how much falls to the wayside.

I have missed countless doctors’ appointments. My vehicle’s license plates have been expired for almost a year. I often apologise to angry friends and acquaintances after they confront me for not seeing them in months. My significant other says she doesn’t see me enough. So do my parents. I clock out of work and shudder at the thought of facing my growing avalanche of text messages. I panic whenever I receive an email that demands I arrange yet another appointment or submit to a lengthy phone call. The stack of forms I’m overdue to submit makes me feel so irresponsible, as if I’m the only adult alive who can’t seem to take care of business.
points: You are not the only one, advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith writes.
It will help to ask whether you have a time problem or a bandwidth problem.

articles.title: Toxic bosses: why do companies protect managers who make working life hell?
articles.summary: Bullying, manipulation and intimidation can destroy lives, yet abusive authoritarians continue to rise to the top. How do they get away with it – and can they be brought to heel? When Andrea finally resigned, her colleagues told her the truth they had always known about her boss. Some apologised.
body: Andrea was a senior legal executive with decades of credibility when she began reporting to a powerful new colleague. Within months, something was wrong. Expectations shifted without warning and feedback contradicted itself. He spoke over her in public and undermined her in private. Slowly she began questioning not just him but herself, her competence, even her grip on reality.

What disturbed Andrea most was the gradual discovery that everybody already knew. Colleagues confessed that when they heard this executive was returning to the organisation, they had cried. When Andrea approached HR, a senior executive told her: “People work longer at McDonald’s than they work for him.” That was acknowledgment, not discovery. And there is something brutally revealing in the stab-vest description. Andrea had become the organisation’s psychological shock absorber. While she took the blows, everybody around her was safer.
points: Bullying, manipulation and intimidation can destroy lives, yet abusive authoritarians continue to rise to the top.
How do they get away with it – and can they be brought to heel?

articles.title: ‘Going places with panache’: Max Mara channels audacious women for Milan show
articles.summary: Chore jackets and loose-fit trousers nod to ‘nonconformist glamour’ of Amelia Earhart and other pioneers. The Max Mara catwalk at Milan fashion week had well-cut coats, sturdy block-heeled boots, crisp white shirts and capacious suede handbags.
body: Trousers were pleated and roomy, skirts long enough to be elegant but not long enough to trip you up. In shades of sand and chalk, grey and black, every piece was designed to work with everything else, and to blend into an existing wardrobe. The styling gestures – a popped collar here, a knotted belt there – stopped short of gimmick. The models could have walked off the runway and on to the Milan street – which, Griffiths said backstage, was the point. “The catwalk show is only the prelude to what to me is the real presentation, which is when I see women walking down the street in my clothes.”

Recently, even this most adult and sensible of brands has sometimes been unable to resist the temptation to chase the youth vote. This season, Max Mara went back to doing what it does best, which is fashion for grownups. (Nothing here for wearing in da club.) Griffiths said: “We were founded on the simple mantra of real clothes for real women, back in the 1960s, and when we stick to that idea, we never go wrong. So more than ever, I wanted to focus on real life chic.”

articles.title: I love seeing pooches in pubs. But not everyone, human or canine, understands the etiquette | Paul Daley
articles.summary: Soon the hounds of Victoria could be formally allowed into watering holes, but brawlers and biters aren’t welcome – neither are misbehaved dogs. Not every dog, just like not every person, should go to the pub. Obstreperous drunks should stay home along with incessant barkers.
body: Soon the dogs of Victoria could be formally allowed into pubs if (and this is a ferociously big if ) the Carroll Labor government is returned at the forthcoming state election. While my blue-heeler-collie-cross Olive – who lives in Sydney but hails from inner-city Melbourne – would, if she could, vote for this amendment to the Food Act 1984, she is also well aware that not every bloke or bitch of her species understands pub etiquette.
There’s no place in her books for growlers and sniffers and frisky types that don’t understand “back off”. Or dogs that won’t get the message either.

Olive can go anywhere. In pubs and restaurants in Sydney’s inner west, where she lives, she will sit contentedly at our feet. She is not food driven. She is not interested in the schnitty and chips at the next table. She’ll gratefully accept a pat but is wary of taking treats from strangers – as we should all perhaps be.
She is well in control of her – ahem! – bodily functions in public places, at all times.

articles.title: All Eyes on Milano: Camera Nazionale della Moda Italiana Celebrated Dalí and Fashion with a Gala Dinner
articles.summary: Mayor Giuseppe Sala welcomed guests including Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Anna Wintour and Vogue Italia’s Francesca Ragazzi, the chief executives of nearly every major Italian fashion house, and designers Brunello Cucinelli, Gianvito Rossi, Alessandro Sartori, and JJ Martin.
body: Less than 24 hours after Vogue World 2026: Milano transformed the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II into a runway, fashion and political leaders reconvened across Piazza del Duomo at Palazzo Reale for the annual Camera Nazionale della Moda Italiana gala dinner ushering in the start of Milan Fashion Week.

Organized by the CNMI with the support of the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation and the Italian Trade Agency, and in collaboration with the Municipality of Milan, the elegant evening also celebrated the opening of the Dalí and Fashion exhibit, whose fashion component was overseen by Vogue World show curator, Judith Clark.

Dalí saw his work in fashion as an extension of his art, and became a regular contributor to Vogue beginning in the mid 1930s, when the magazine commissioned him to illustrate a red chiffon evening gown. He conceived the image as a photo-painting, placing the model in one of his stark Surrealist landscapes. His first Vogue cover followed in 1939, featuring a woman whose head dissolves into flowers, with two subsequent covers in 1944 and 1946, alongside fashion illustrations.

articles.title: King Princess Brought Her Mom as Her Plus-One to Jil Sander
articles.summary: King Princess—and her mom, Aggie—bring Vogue along on their mother-daughter trip to the Jil Sander spring 2027 show in Milan.
body: While one might expect the musician to have a highly curated playlist bumping while she gets ready for the Jil Sander spring 2027 show, KP actually prefers a more relaxed hair and makeup routine. “I like to sit in complete silence and get my face painted,” she tells Vogue. “It’s wonderful and meditative.”

After glam is finished—which includes her “pretty extensive skin-care routine”—it’s time to get dressed. King Princess’s selected look from the fall 2026 collection: a lush double-breasted camel coat with a pair of navy trousers, with—Simone Bellotti’s signature touch—a half-tucked collar. Straight away, the singer saw the rock-and-roll potential in the look. “I saw this coat and thought to myself, This is fierce,” she says. “It feels like Marc Bolan would wear this on a T. Rex album cover.”

articles.title: How to Find the Perfect Semi-Formal Wedding Guest Dress
articles.summary: Looking for a semi-formal wedding guest dress? We found 24 options from brands like Tove, Staud, and Fforme that are perfectly suited to the occasion.
body: A black-tie invite tells you exactly what to do: gown, heels, done. “Formal” calls for polished, occasion-ready looks; “ cocktail ” has its own well-worn (and self-explanatory) rules. But semi-formal attire? This directive sits in a gray zone, making it one of the easiest wedding style choices to overthink; as a bridal stylist, it’s the dress code my clients (and my group chats) text me the most about.

Proenza Schouler’s red-and-blue dress, Tove’s turquoise maxi, and Massimo Dutti’s flowing bohemian style all make strong cases for a bolder take on semi-formal wedding guest dressing. For the minimalists, the LBD has a place here, too: Khaite’s strapless midi, Chloé’s lace-trimmed slip, and Staud’s one-shoulder number are all sharp alternatives to the usual wedding-guest uniform, proving that classic doesn’t have to mean predictable.
Ultimately, building a semi-formal wardrobe starts with knowing where to shop, so here are 24 pieces worth having on rotation.
